_comment: Prompt manifest for build/gen-art.py. Edit subjects/aspect here; the style_prefix and negative apply to every slot so the placeholder set stays coherent. IDs match the slots wired into build-pdf.sh + the shot list in '../Art Direction & Placement Plan.md'. Diagrams F1-F7 and icons I1 are NOT here on purpose — those are hand-built as SVG by Claude, not generated. Aspect ratios use Gemini's supported set (1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9).
style_prefix: Loose black-and-white pen-and-ink sketch illustration, hand-drawn linework with light cross-hatching and gestural shading, high contrast, plain white background. Rough, energetic indie-RPG interior art in the spirit of Dungeon World and Monster of the Week. Grayscale only, no color. Cinematic framing, all-ages but not childish. No text, no lettering, no borders.
negative: color, photorealistic, 3D render, glossy, painterly, watermark, signature, text, letters, words, logos, frame, page border, cluttered background, anime, chibi, cutesy cartoon

C1.note: cover is normally COLOR + designer-led; this is a grayscale concept placeholder only
C1.subject: An ensemble of adventurers striking a dynamic hero pose as a film spotlight and clapperboard frame the scene; energetic, poster-like.

C2.subject: A group of friends in a director's writing room gathered around a big table, rolling dice and acting out a scene they are writing together — one person leaping up mid-performance, another laughing, a third scribbling notes; storyboards, script pages, and a clapperboard scattered around. The tabletop as a movie writers' room. Warm, human, tone-setting.

D1.subject: Friends around a tabletop mid-game, dice rolling, and imaginative shapes (a dragon, a rocket) rising like smoke from the table. Warm and welcoming.

D2.subject: Two oversized six-sided dice tumbling through the air with motion lines, dramatic and kinetic.

D3.subject: An open book or unrolled map from which genre scenes swirl outward — a castle, a ray-gun, a haunted house, a ruined city. A montage of possibility.

D4.subject: A director's desk and open toolbox: scattered dice, character sheets, a pencil, a spotlight, index cards. Reference-and-tools feel.

G1.subject: Heroes crossing a fraying rope bridge over a deep chasm toward a ruined jungle temple, a glint of treasure ahead. Sweeping, pulpy adventure.

G2.subject: A detective bent over a clue-strewn desk with a magnifying glass, rain streaking a window, long noir shadows.

G3.subject: A lone figure with a flashlight in a doorway; a huge shadow or half-seen creature looms beyond. Dread, heavy negative space.

G4.subject: Space explorers in suits dwarfed before a towering alien monolith under a vast field of stars. Awe and scale.

G5.subject: A crew mid-heist rappelling toward a vault past a laser grid, sly confident grins, stylish and slick.

G6.subject: A charged face-to-face confrontation between two characters under a single theatrical spotlight, high emotion. Not cozy.

G7.subject: A lone wanderer in makeshift gear standing on a ridge, overlooking a ruined, overgrown city skyline at dusk.

O1.subject: A horizontal strip of film with a few tiny scene frames inside it and a spotlight glow at one end. A slim reusable banner motif.

S1a.subject: Two or three players laughing around dice and snacks at a table, one hand mid-roll.

S1b.subject: A single confident hero character portrait, half-length, publicity-still framing.

S1c.subject: A menacing dust storm or roiling plague cloud with a face barely suggested within it.

S1d.subject: Weary heroes regrouping around a small campfire, catching their breath.

S1e.subject: Characters in a dynamic, dramatic retreat, glancing back over a shoulder.

S1f.subject: A hand releasing two six-sided dice in mid-air, motion lines, tension.

slots._vignette_comment: V1-V24 are small square SCENE vignettes composited into the fixed film-strip chapter opener (build/compose-strip.py + build/deal-openers.py deals 3 per chapter). Prompts force a single centered subject on a mostly-white ground with minimal shading, so they read cleanly inside a tiny frame window and sit uniformly in the strip.
